Impact: live checkout failures impacting revenue. We need either a fast failover to a compatible model variant or a capacity/fix to restore throughput.

Please advise urgently.

Thanks,

Subject: URGENT: Aurora Payments checkout 502/latency spike — triage

Vivek / Rishi — Aurora (PD-8812) reporting ~18% 502s and ~45% throughput drop on calls to model-redwood-v4. Customer is in prod (high priority). I pulled initial edge traces and see:

- Large number of upstream TCP retransmits to our egress proxies for Aurora CIDRs starting 08:48 PT
- DNS lookups for model-redwood-v4 are returning intermittently with ~300-400ms resolution, plus ~10% NXDOMAIN spikes for A records (lookups land on our proxy egress)
- Proxy logs show a tail of 504s and connection timeouts; there are periodic resets from an intermediate firewall/NAT device (src port churn)

Attachments: tcpdump-aurora.pcap (compressed) — a 30s capture showing SYN retries and multiple RSTs to same 10.8.x.1 egress IP.

Ask: please triage ASAP and advise one of the following by 09:45 PT:
- Short-term mitigation (route lift, alternative egress IP/region, config tweak)
- If customer-side rate/changes detected, confirm and advise

Marissa — please prep an external update template in case we need to communicate an ETA to Aurora execs.

Thanks,
Olga

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:38:54 -07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: Aurora Payments checkout 502/latency spike — triage

Quick triage summary (from edge + egress teams):

Findings:
- Observed SNAT port exhaustion on our primary NAT gateway in us-west-2 during 08:45–09:05 PT. Connections to Aurora's CIDR were being queued; many attempts fell back to a secondary proxy which intermittently dropped connections (504s).
- DNS lookups were reattempted and occasionally resolved to a deprecated egress IP that had an ACL applied earlier today — the ACL caused silent drops for some TCP flows (explains NXDOMAIN-like behavior in app traces).
- No model-serving throttles or overloaded GPUs found on Redwood side.

Immediate mitigations applied (09:28–09:36 PT):
1) Increased NAT ephemeral port allocation and added an additional NAT instance in the us-west-2 pool (hot-add).
2) Rotated egress route to prefer an alternate proxy cluster that was healthy (failover).
3) Pushed a temporary firewall ACL rollback for the deprecated egress IPs that were applied during a config push at 07:50 PT.

Result: request success rate improved to ~97% by 09:35 PT; throughput increased back to ~90% of baseline by 09:40 PT. Still monitoring for residual DNS cache effects.

Follow-ups (owners):
- Infra (Vivek) to run postmortem on NAT scaling and autoscale thresholds (owner: Vivek).
- Network config team to review change that introduced deprecated egress IP ACL (owner: Rishi).
- CS/AM (Marissa) to coordinate a customer postmortem and credit discussion.

I'm standing by if you want me to join a call with Aurora.

Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 13:02:11 -07:00
Subject: Aurora incident update — mitigation applied; next steps

Claire — update and apologies for the disruption this morning. Summary:

- Root cause (preliminary): capacity/config edge interaction — SNAT port exhaustion combined with a mistaken ACL on a deprecated egress IP caused connection drops and DNS resolution fallbacks that led to elevated 502/504s.
- Mitigation performed (09:28–09:36 PT): added NAT capacity, hot-added alternate NAT instance, rotated traffic to healthy proxy cluster, and rolled back the ACL change.
- Current status: success rate restored to >98%, throughput within 95% of baseline. Our monitoring shows no new spikes in the last 30 minutes.

Attachments: incident-timeline.pdf (timeline and preliminary notes), tcpdump excerpt.

Next steps:
1) We will run a full RCA and share a postmortem by EOD Monday (owner: Infra).
2) We'll propose a compensating credit consistent with our SLA; Marissa will follow up on specifics.
3) Engineering will adjust NAT autoscale thresholds and add a preventive test in our e2e harness that simulates CIDR-heavy traffic.

If Aurora would like a short incident-briefing call this afternoon I'm available 15:30–16:30 PT. Marissa will work with you to schedule.

Again — very sorry. We understand the impact and are treating this as a P1.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Head of Customer Escalations
Redwood Inference
